content:
Two years ago when Apple launched the M4 Mac mini, teardown reports immediately brought good news: the internal SSD was not soldered to the motherboard, allowing users to upgrade storage capacity later. We even did a tutorial demonstration.

However, the latest M6 and M5 Pro versions of the Mac mini appear to have the storage chips soldered back onto the motherboard.

The new Mac mini's storage chips are once again permanently soldered, a step backward for upgradability

Expand Mac mini revealed in a blog post that this time the NAND chips are again soldered to the motherboard, similar to the situation with the M1 and M2 Mac mini, meaning the SSD module cannot be removed.

Expand Mac mini has been selling upgrade storage modules for the M4 and M4 Pro Mac mini, but they stated that based on the current situation, "support for the M6 and M5 Pro appears unlikely to materialize."

Without slots, there's nothing to swap out, and there's very little room for us to work with. Back in August we said we'd wait until we had hands-on testing before expanding support. Now the results are in, and they're not what we hoped for. We'll continue to look for solutions, but support for the M6 and M5 Pro doesn't look promising. If the situation changes, we'll let everyone know here first.

For comparison, Expand Mac mini's 1TB SSD expansion module (for the M4 Mac mini) is priced at USD 300; Apple charges USD 500 to upgrade the M6 Mac mini from 256GB to 1TB. Expand Mac mini's 2TB module is priced at USD 420, while Apple's upgrade fee is USD 1,000.

As for the Mac Studio, Apple's repair guide still shows a removable SSD design, but we have yet to see any teardown reports confirming this.

If you have an M4 Mac mini and want to upgrade the storage, you can refer to the detailed step-by-step tutorial written by 9to5Mac's Jeff Benjamin.

Although it's not the same as an internal storage upgrade, Satechi has released a thoughtful accessory with a built-in SSD enclosure that also provides additional ports for the M6 Mac mini.
